candidate.eventStartRule: The official registry timestamp of independently corroborated debug@4.4.2 defines the strict cutoff; independent reports document the 8 September 2025 compromise context but do not substitute for the registry timestamp.

maintainerIncidentIssue.statement: The Debug project issue identifies debug@4.4.2 among affected releases and reports a phishing-driven npm account compromise.

wizTechnicalReport.statement: Wiz identifies debug@4.4.2 in its exact affected-version list and describes control of the maintainer npm account through social engineering.

stepSecurityTechnicalReport.statement: StepSecurity identifies debug@4.4.2 in its confirmed affected-version list and describes the phishing attack on the maintainer.

nextDecisionBoundary: The candidate may proceed to a separate governed reconstruction only after all ledger-dependent artifacts are updated atomically and the shared-campaign family boundary is retained.
prohibitedInterpretations: This evidence screen does not establish campaign completeness, common actor identity beyond the documented maintainer-compromise context, causality, or statistical independence among package rows.
No later package, repository, maintainer, workflow, lockfile, download, payload, installation, or dependency-reach state may be substituted for the selected strict pre-event source object.

An eligible source-object screen alone does not create a cutoff-valid control population, benign labels, historical installation trace, dependency reach, blast-radius estimate, score, model, ranking, interval, calibration result, or predictive metric.
